summary: Defines a PCEP extension that associates two or more LSPs so they act as working and protection paths for one another under an active stateful PCE. This lets a controller set up and manage backup paths that take over if the primary path fails.

eli5.summary: A school bus route has a main road and a backup road. This tells the central planner which path is the main one and which is the spare.

questions: how to associate working and protection lsps in pcep
what is path protection association in pcep
what is a path protection association group
subtitle: A way for a PCE and its routers to group a working LSP with its protection LSPs so backups can be planned and controlled together.

tldr.problem: When a stateful PCE controls a working LSP, it is useful for the same PCE to compute and control the protection LSPs that take over when it fails. PCEP needed a way to say which LSPs protect which.
tldr.mechanism: It defines the Path Protection Association type (value 1) for the generic ASSOCIATION object, and a Path Protection Association TLV (type 38) whose flags mark each LSP as working or protection, primary or secondary, and give the protection type.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 9756. PCCs and PCEs can now report, create and update a protection group, and reject malformed groups with defined errors.

today: RFC 8745 is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 9756, so read the two together. The text of this RFC does not say how widely it is deployed.

sections.title: Protecting LSPs with a Stateful PCE
sections.content:
In path protection, a working LSP is protected by one or more protection LSPs that are activated when the working LSP fails. When the working LSPs are computed and controlled by a PCE, it helps if the same PCE also computes and controls the protection LSPs. This document gives PCEP a way to associate two or more LSPs for that purpose.

It covers three cases: a PCC initiates a protection LSP and keeps control (passive stateful mode); a PCC initiates it and delegates control to the PCE (active stateful mode); or the PCE initiates it (PCE-initiated mode). A protection LSP can be signaled before the failure, as a standby or primary LSP, or after the failure, as a secondary LSP. Which to use is an operator choice or policy.
sections.eli5: Imagine two roads to school, a main one and a spare. The planner needs to know that the two roads belong together, so it can switch if the main road is blocked.

sections.title: The Path Protection Association Group
sections.content:
RFC 8697 defines a generic way to group LSPs: instead of listing the other LSPs it interacts with, each LSP individually joins an association group via the ASSOCIATION object. This RFC defines Association type 1, the Path Protection Association Type, and the resulting Path Protection Association Group (PPAG).

A member can be a working or protection LSP. A PPAG can have one working LSP and/or one or more protection LSPs. The source, destination, Tunnel ID and Protection Type of all LSPs in a PPAG MUST be the same. The association is dynamic and is created by the PCC or the PCE for LSPs of the same TE tunnel. By default the association source is the address of the local PCEP speaker that created it. An operator-configured Association Range MUST NOT be set for this type and MUST be ignored.

A speaker MAY list type 1 in the ASSOC-Type-List TLV of its OPEN object before using PPAGs.
sections.eli5: Each path joins a club. Every member of the club has the same start and finish, and the club knows which one is the main path.

sections.title: The Path Protection Association TLV
sections.content:
This optional TLV goes in the ASSOCIATION object and MUST NOT appear more than once; only the first is processed. It has Type 38 and a fixed Length of 4. Its value is one 32-bit flags field.

  • P (Protecting): 0 means a working LSP, 1 means a protection LSP.
  • S (Secondary): 0 means primary, 1 means secondary. It is ignored if P is not set.
  • PT (Protection Type): 6 bits, as defined for the LSP protection type flags in RFC 4872. Any value usable in the RSVP-TE PROTECTION object is acceptable unless stated otherwise.

Unassigned bits MUST be 0 on transmission and ignored on receipt. If the TLV is missing, the LSP is treated as a working LSP.
sections.eli5: Each path wears a name tag with two tick boxes: is it the spare, and is it the first or second spare. There is also a code for what kind of protection it gives.

sections.title: How Associations Are Used
sections.content:
All procedures and error handling for the ASSOCIATION object follow RFC 8697. During state synchronization a PCC reports its LSPs and their association memberships, including PPAGs.

For PCC-initiated LSPs, the PCC can add LSPs to a PPAG or remove them and reports the change in a PCRpt message. It can also delegate the working and protection LSPs to an active stateful PCE, which can then update their paths and attributes, and the association, with PCUpd. Both should be delegated together and to the same PCE to avoid race conditions.

For PCE-initiated LSPs, the PCE can create and update working and protection LSPs independently, remove a protection LSP from a PPAG, and send association information in PCUpd or PCInitiate messages.

When a session ends, association information is cleared along with the LSP state. At the PCC this happens after the State Timeout Interval expires. A group with no LSPs left is considered deleted.
sections.eli5: The router tells the planner who is in each club. The planner can add or remove spare paths, as long as the same planner looks after the main and the spare.

sections.title: Error Handling
sections.content:
Failures use PCErr with Error-Type 26 (Association Error) from RFC 8697. A speaker that does not support the type returns Error-Value 1. This RFC adds three values: 9 for a Tunnel ID or endpoints mismatch, 10 for an attempt to add another working or protection LSP, and 11 for an unsupported protection type. Mismatched Protection Type values, or a conflict between two PPAGs, give Error-Value 6 (Association information mismatch).

Limits depend on the protection type. For 1+1 (protection type 0x08 or 0x10), a PPAG can hold at most one working LSP and one protection LSP. For 1:N (0x04), it can hold at most one protection LSP and no more than N working LSPs. These checks MUST NOT be applied during make-before-break, when two paths briefly coexist. A given LSP MAY belong to more than one PPAG. An LSP-IDENTIFIERS TLV SHOULD be included for all LSPs.
sections.eli5: If someone tries to put a path in the wrong club, or add a third spare where only one is allowed, the other side says no and gives a reason code.

sections.title: Security and Related Work
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 8231, RFC 8281 and RFC 5440 apply, plus the association-related ones in RFC 8697. A spurious protection LSP added to a PPAG could give a false sense of reliability, which hurts when the working LSP and the protection LSP both fail. Securing the PCEP session with TLS (RFC 8253) is RECOMMENDED.

Working and protection LSPs are typically resource disjoint, so one failure does not affect both. That requirement is handled by a separate Disjointness Association, described in an Internet-Draft, and not by this document. The Path Protection Association TLV information from the PCE is used to trigger signaling of the working and protection LSPs, with flags mapped to the RSVP-TE PROTECTION object.
sections.eli5: A fake spare path would make everyone feel safe when they are not, so the conversation between planner and router should be locked.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Fixed length of the value in octets.

items.label: Association type not supported
items.desc: Peer does not support the Path Protection type.

items.label: Association information mismatch
items.desc: Protection Type differs, or two PPAGs conflict.

items.label: Tunnel ID or endpoints mismatch
items.desc: LSP does not match the PPAG tunnel, source or destination.

items.label: Another working/protection LSP
items.desc: Too many LSPs for the protection type.

items.label: Protection type not supported
items.desc: Peer cannot handle the type set in the PPAG.
